_README: The `sales` fixture's SEMANTIC LAYER — the layer-on arm of the eval A/B (`--semantic on`). Written by hand, never generated, so the arm is deterministic and costs no tokens to set up. THE AUTHORING RULE, and the only thing that keeps this arm honest: every claim here is the structured form of a fact already stated in sales_seed.sql or sales_comments.sql. Nothing was written by reading app/eval/suites/sales_v1.json — a layer authored against the gold answers measures the author, not the feature. The two deliberate plants in the comments overlay (customers.segment stale, orders.subtotal wrong) are carried here in their TRUE form: this layer is human-curated and reviewed, which is exactly the difference between it and a DDL comment that rotted. `joins` is empty on purpose — app.semantic.derive_joins reads cardinality and fan-out off the catalog at load time, which is what the product does too, so the fan-out cautions in the rendered block are derived from the fixture rather than typed here. The runner binds this document to the live snapshot with validate_document() and REFUSES TO RUN if any entry is invalid: a half-resolving layer is a measurement of nothing.
business_context: Order-to-cash for the online storefront: catalogue, customers, orders, fulfilment and returns. Loaded nightly from the ERP; the current day is always partial until the 03:00 UTC run.
default_exclusions: closed customer accounts (customers.is_deleted = true), and the deprecated public.product table, whose six rows are a 2019 migration leftover.

time.notes: the nightly load lands at 03:00 UTC, so today is always partial

entities.label: Orders
entities.description: One row per checkout, at any stage of its life. Cancelled and returned orders keep their money on them.
entities.grain: one row per customer order

columns.name: status
columns.label: Order status
columns.description: Where the order got to. Not every order is a sale

columns.name: channel
columns.label: Sales channel
columns.description: web is the storefront, phone is taken by a rep, partner is a reseller's system

columns.name: total_amount
columns.label: Order total
columns.description: What the customer was billed: subtotal less discount, plus tax and shipping. This is the revenue figure for an order

columns.name: subtotal
columns.label: Goods value
columns.description: The value of the lines before discount, tax and shipping. Not what the customer paid — that is total_amount

columns.name: order_date
columns.label: Order date
columns.description: The calendar day the order was placed; placed_at is the same event with a timestamp

columns.name: employee_id
columns.label: Rep
columns.description: The rep who booked it, NULL for web orders — an inner join here drops the storefront

columns.name: cust_ref
columns.label: Legacy reference
columns.description: Reference from the OMS retired in 2022. Sparse and not a key — never join on it

metrics.name: revenue
metrics.label: Revenue
metrics.description: what the customer was billed, tax and shipping included

metrics.name: order_count
metrics.label: Orders
metrics.description: counted DISTINCT so a join to the lines cannot inflate it

metrics.name: discount_given
metrics.label: Discount given
metrics.description: money taken off by promotions and coupons together

entities.label: Order lines
entities.description: The bridge between the catalogue and revenue: anything about products, brands, suppliers or tags reaches orders only through here.
entities.grain: one row per product line on an order

columns.name: line_total
columns.label: Line value
columns.description: quantity x unit_price after the line's discount. Summed over an order this gives its subtotal, not its total_amount

columns.name: unit_price
columns.label: Unit price
columns.description: the price at the time of sale, which can differ from products.price today

columns.name: discount
columns.label: Line discount
columns.description: percent off this line, already reflected in line_total — do not subtract it twice

columns.name: variant_id
columns.label: Variant
columns.description: the colour/size variant sold, NULL on lines sold at product level

metrics.name: line_revenue
metrics.label: Line revenue
metrics.description: the goods value of the lines; an order's tax and shipping are not in here

entities.label: Payments
entities.description: Money received against an order. Only fulfilled orders have one.
entities.grain: one row per capture against an order

columns.name: amount
columns.label: Amount captured
columns.description: in the order's currency. One payment per order — instalments were never migrated

columns.name: paid_at
columns.label: Captured at
columns.description: up to three days after the order was placed; use orders.order_date for when the sale happened

columns.name: status
columns.label: Settlement state
columns.description: everything here is captured; authorised-only and failed attempts live in the gateway

metrics.name: amount_captured
metrics.label: Amount captured
metrics.description: cash received, which is not the same as revenue booked

entities.label: Returns
entities.description: One row per returned order line. Only approved returns produce a refund.
entities.grain: one row per returned order line

columns.name: status
columns.label: Return status
columns.description: approved or rejected; only approved ones are refunded

columns.name: refund_amount
columns.label: Credited
columns.description: what was credited for the returned units, before any restocking fee

columns.name: reason
columns.label: Reason
columns.description: free text from a fixed list — treat it as a label, not a code

metrics.name: credited_amount
metrics.label: Credited
metrics.description: what an approved return was worth; refunds.amount is what actually left the account

entities.label: Refunds
entities.description: Money sent back for an approved return.
entities.grain: one row per refund paid out

columns.name: payment_id
columns.label: Original capture
columns.description: NULL for store-credit refunds, which are tied to no capture

metrics.name: refunded
metrics.label: Refunded
metrics.description: money that actually left the account

entities.label: Shipments
entities.description: One dispatch from a warehouse. An order can ship in several consignments.
entities.grain: one row per consignment

columns.name: delivered_at
columns.label: Delivered at
columns.description: NULL while the consignment is still in transit

columns.name: status
columns.label: Shipment status
columns.description: delivered once the carrier confirmed, in_transit until then

metrics.name: shipment_count
metrics.label: Shipments
metrics.description: consignments, not orders — an order can ship more than once

entities.label: Product reviews
entities.grain: one row per customer review of a product

columns.name: rating
columns.label: Stars
columns.description: 1 to 5, whole numbers; 1 is the worst

columns.name: is_hidden
columns.label: Hidden by moderation
columns.description: true for reviews moderation pulled; they stay in the table

columns.name: customer_id
columns.label: Author
columns.description: NULL when the review was left anonymously

metrics.name: average_rating
metrics.label: Average rating
metrics.description: moderated-out reviews are not part of a public average

entities.label: Support tickets
entities.description: Not every contact is about an order.
entities.grain: one row per customer contact

columns.name: status
columns.label: Ticket status
columns.description: open and pending are still with us; resolved and closed are finished, and only those carry closed_at

columns.name: order_id
columns.label: Order
columns.description: NULL for pre-sales and account questions

entities.label: Customers
entities.description: Rows are never deleted; is_deleted marks a closed account.
entities.grain: one row per customer account

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.label: Account closed
columns.description: soft delete — about 8% of the table, kept for the order history hanging off it

columns.name: segment
columns.label: Commercial segment
columns.description: how the account is managed

columns.name: last_order_at
columns.label: Last order
columns.description: refreshed by the nightly load; NULL for accounts that never ordered

columns.name: credit_limit
columns.label: Credit limit
columns.description: a commercial term — it says nothing about what the customer has bought

columns.name: referred_by_id
columns.label: Referred by
columns.description: the existing customer who referred this one; self-referencing and mostly NULL

entities.label: Products
entities.description: The sellable catalogue, current and retired.
entities.grain: one row per sellable product

columns.name: price
columns.label: List price
columns.description: current list price before any promotion; what a line actually sold at is order_items.unit_price

columns.name: cost
columns.label: Unit cost
columns.description: what we pay our supplier per unit; margin is price - cost. NULL where we never bought directly

columns.name: category
columns.label: Legacy category label
columns.description: denormalised text kept for the old reporting stack and not maintained. category_id is the real relationship

columns.name: discontinued
columns.label: Withdrawn
columns.description: true once withdrawn from sale for good; withdrawn products keep their order history

columns.name: flg_2
columns.label: Legacy flag
columns.description: meaning lost; never filter on it

entities.label: Product (deprecated)
entities.description: The 2019 migration leftover. The live catalogue is public.products.
entities.grain: six stale rows from the 2019 migration — the live catalogue is public.products, and nothing here belongs in an answer

entities.label: Employees
entities.grain: one row per member of sales staff

columns.name: terminated_at
columns.label: Left on
columns.description: set once they have left; NULL for current staff

columns.name: salary
columns.label: Base salary
columns.description: annual base excluding commission. Confidential — aggregate it, do not list it per person

columns.name: commission_pct
columns.label: Commission rate
columns.description: on booked revenue; 0 for staff not on a commission plan

columns.name: manager_id
columns.label: Manager
columns.description: self-referencing; NULL for the six people at the top

entities.label: Sales territories
entities.description: How the business slices the world. A region groups a country but is not one.
entities.grain: one row per sales territory

columns.name: country_id
columns.label: Country
columns.description: NULL for legacy territories such as Unassigned

entities.label: Stock on hand
entities.description: A snapshot of now, overwritten by the warehouse feed.
entities.grain: one row per product per warehouse, with no history — it cannot answer a question about a past date

columns.name: quantity
columns.label: Units on hand
columns.description: physically on the shelf, including units already allocated to an unshipped order

columns.name: reorder_level
columns.label: Reorder level
columns.description: the level at which purchasing is prompted; a threshold, not a target

entities.label: Suppliers
entities.grain: one row per supplier

columns.name: lead_time_days
columns.label: Lead time
columns.description: contracted working days from purchase order to delivery; product_suppliers overrides it per product

columns.name: rating
columns.label: Supplier score
columns.description: internal, 1 to 5, reviewed quarterly. Not a customer-facing rating

entities.label: Promotions
entities.description: Marketing campaigns. A promotion reaches an order through order_promotions or through a coupon; the two paths overlap.
entities.grain: one row per marketing campaign

columns.name: discount_pct
columns.label: Headline discount
columns.description: for percent-type promotions only; ignored for bogo and fixed

entities.label: Promotions applied
entities.grain: one row per promotion applied to an order — an order can carry several

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.label: Attributed discount
columns.description: the part of the order's discount_total this promotion accounts for

entities.label: Product sourcing
entities.grain: one row per product per supplier — most products have two, so joining it to order lines multiplies revenue

entities.label: Merchandising tags
entities.grain: one row per tag on a product — a product carries about four, so a per-tag total counts one sale once per tag

entities.label: Team membership
entities.grain: one row per rep per team — some reps sit in two, so revenue by team will not add up to company revenue

entities.label: Daily sales rollup
entities.description: Convenient and dangerous: rebuilt nightly for the trailing 90 days only.
entities.grain: one row per region per day, for the TRAILING 90 DAYS ONLY — anything reaching further back must be answered from orders and order_items

columns.name: gross_revenue
columns.label: Gross revenue
columns.description: sum of order_items.line_total for that region and day; refunds are not netted off

columns.name: refunds_total
columns.label: Refunds
columns.description: not populated by the current job — read it as zero, not as no refunds

glossary.meaning: orders.total_amount summed — what customers were billed. Line-level questions use order_items.line_total, which excludes tax and shipping
order_items.quantity, never a count of order lines
an order that reached completed, shipped or returned — the states that have a payment against them
revenue less refunds.amount over the same period; nothing in the schema stores it
